workload.inputs: Two independent finite torch.randn tensors from one seeded device generator; unnormalized log-probabilities.

methodology.isolation: One fresh subprocess per method, run sequentially.
methodology.timing: Median perf_counter walltime after warmup; CUDA synchronized before and after each call. Excludes setup, input construction, and memory sampling.
methodology.memory: First reduction before warmup; subtract pre-call memory with both input tensors already resident. CPU uses sampled RSS; CUDA uses PyTorch peak allocated bytes.
limits: Synthetic finite inputs measure reduction cost only, not end-to-end model performance.
Identical RNG seed and construction are used in both workers; random values may differ across devices, dtypes, or PyTorch versions.
Small shapes can be dominated by launch, thread, or Python overhead; timing and memory are separate passes.

limitations: RSS is an estimate of resident process memory, not tensor allocation bytes.
Sampling and OS scheduling can miss short-lived peaks, especially for small workloads.
Allocator reuse, residency changes, and sampler overhead affect the delta; a zero delta does not imply zero allocations.
